niche: an Australian distribution network's rooftop PV forecast for its FY2027-28 capital program: which of the eight 22 kV feeders out of one peri-urban zone substation gets the single accelerated hosting-capacity upgrade, sized on rooftop PV connected at 31 August 2029, when the city council runs solar bulk-buys this spring in a large, slow-adopting new estate and a smaller, fast-adopting one
answer: YRB27 should get the accelerated hosting capacity augmentation in the FY2027-28 capital works program. Its rooftop PV will sit 1.9 MW above its hosting capacity at 31 August 2029, 0.5 MW more than YRB24's 1.4 MW, because the Wattleview bulk-buy will add 1.7 MW to it.

driver: A scheduled intervention's increment at a new site is carried from its past runs as a multiple of the site's own recent rate of the outcome, rebuilt per site behind a three-file join; every share of a pool (contacted, eligible, eligible and not yet responded) scatters several-fold across the past runs and hands the site with the largest untouched but slow pool several times its increment, so the call goes to that site instead of the fast one.
driver_concrete: Each of the council's seven past solar bulk-buys installed about 1.17 systems for every first rooftop PV application its suburb's owner-occupied houses lodged in the year before sign-ups opened (1.03 to 1.35), a count rebuilt from the connection register through the rates roll and the NMI-to-property cross-reference, while per home letterboxed, per owner-occupied house or per house still without PV they scatter several-fold; Wattleview (209 first applications a year) adds 1.7 MW to YRB27 and Bindarra Waters (52, on a pool twice the size) 0.4 MW to YRB24, so YRB27 is furthest over hosting capacity in August 2029, where every pool basis puts YRB24 first.
stump: A competent solver carries the past bulk-buys per home letterboxed and files YRB24 at about 1.8 MW over hosting capacity, and the textbook correction per owner-occupied house still without PV files YRB24 at 3.0; the step that lands both there is carrying a campaign's yield on a pool of houses instead of on the suburb's own uptake (about 1.17 systems per first application in the year before sign-ups opened), which gives Bindarra Waters' large, slow estate two to five times its campaign: the golden is YRB27 at about 1.9 MW.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads the forecasting procedure, collapses alterations, joins legacy inverters, places NMIs on the network model and pools the past campaigns' rate per home letterboxed files YRB24 at about 1.8 MW; per owner-occupied house still without PV (the textbook reflex) files YRB24 at 3.0, and fitted models on penetration, pool, letterboxes and houses file YRB24 at 1.7 to 2.9.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each feeder's design-point rooftop PV against its spring minimum-demand hosting capacity, with a council bulk-buy's increment forecast as an uplift on the suburb's own baseline uptake estimated from past programs, which is how DER forecasters carry a program's increment; with another field's nouns, inverter ratings, hosting capacity, rooftop PV applications and the embedded generation register have nothing to attach to.

lineage.driver: A scheduled intervention's yield is carried to new sites from its past runs, and it is stable only per member who can still respond, those inside the intervention's area who qualify and have not already responded, a pool built by joining a membership roll through a link file to the response log; per contacted member, per qualifying member, per member without a response or per whole site each fits the past runs no better than the raw counts, so every such transfer leaves the site with the largest untouched pool at a third to a half of its yield and the call with a rival.

notes: Calibration none: the seven past campaigns are the distributor's and the council's own history from which the program component is estimated, not an organ confirming a filed criterion.
